proposed.demonstrated_gap: Skills reach each client and worker only as filesystem copies. Claude gets copies from tools/adoption/install_skills.py, and Codex reads those copies by absolute path through skills.config (adoption/skills/lifecycle.md:64-69). The runtime-worker trial installs 137 skills from 13 sources for OpenHands workers, and worker discovery there is unmeasured (blueprints/runtime-workers/skills/README.md). The official Skills over MCP extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/skills; SEP-2640 Final; maintained by the Skills Over MCP Working Group) lists skills by metadata and serves SKILL.md and supporting files only when needed. It adds digest and manifest verification, origin binding and per-skill approval. One pinned skill server could then give each role-scoped Claude, Codex or SDK worker its skill set without copying catalogs into every client. It is not usable here yet. The installed Claude Code 2.1.291 binary contains a client: a capability check on extensions['io.modelcontextprotocol/skills'], plus listMcpSkillPage, which sends skills/list. That client is gated by the tengu_mcp_skills flag, which defaults to false, and no CHANGELOG entry mentions it. The Codex 0.160.1 binary does not contain the identifier. The official Python and TypeScript SDK work is still in open PRs (python-sdk #3485, typescript-sdk #2818). The client matrix lists ChatGPT, fast-agent and MCP Inspector as partial and mcpc as full, with no Claude Code or Codex row. Microsoft Agent Framework .NET's experimental UseMcpSkills reads a skill://index.json index, the pre-final shape.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Open gap 1 still has no optimizer arm. microsoft/skillopt was refuted, and no winner (ECC, TypeSafe, OpenAI skills) shows a measured task-quality gain: wave 2 scored 10/12 against 10/12, wave 3 14/16 against 14/16. GEPA optimize_anything optimizes any text artifact, including a SKILL.md, from a seed, an evaluator, an objective and max_metric_calls (README L111-131). GEPA also ships its own Claude Code skill and plugin to drive it (gepa-optimize-anything, README L133-142), so only the evaluator that scores a candidate with this stack's arms is glue. Published evidence on held-out sets: the maintainer's gskill blog reports test resolve rates rising from 55% to 82% (Jinja) and from 24% to 93% (Bleve) with mini-SWE-agent. The skills transferred to Claude Code: Haiku 4.5 rose from 79.3% to 100% on Bleve, while Sonnet 4.5 had saturated, so only duration fell. An independent study (arXiv 2609.12742, 2026-09-11) finds +4.9pp for GEPA and +0.1pp for SkillOpt across three repositories, but cannot separate the GEPA gain from run-to-run variance. Design correction: the frozen case set cannot decide the outcome. C1-C4 sit at 2/2 in both arms, which skill-creator's analyzer.md L214-218 calls non-discriminating; only C5 and C6 have headroom (at most +2/12), and the set has no held-out split. It serves only as a no-regression guard. Maintenance: 40 default-branch commits since 2026-08-01 (33 non-bot), the latest on 2026-10-01. Release v0.1.4 lags the branch, so pin commit fb1ed589fd83. The reflection LM is a LiteLLM model string (README L88, L106) that can point at the existing OmniRoute gateway, so no new credentials are needed; that path is untested.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: The arms, metric and decision rule follow skill-creator at anthropics/skills@8a1541c4. Three arms run together on the same model, prompt and tools: without_skill (Skill tool disallowed), old_skill (a byte-pinned snapshot of the seed, the skill-creator baseline rule for improving an existing skill) and gepa_skill. Seed: one pinned SKILL.md with headroom. Decision set: at least 60 non-saturated tasks mined as merged PRs reverted at a frozen base commit (the arXiv 2609.12742 method), from this repository or nautilus_trader, with the repository's own checks as the oracle. Split train, validation and held-out test the way gskill split about 200/50/60. GEPA never sees the test split, and its internal validation score only selects the candidate. Run at least 3 runs per case per arm. Grade with grading.json {text,passed,evidence} and the blind comparator in agents/comparator.md (wave 3 flagged the missing blind judge as major), then aggregate with scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py for pass_rate, time and tokens as mean±stddev with deltas. Drop ceiling cases from the decision metric. Adopt only if gepa_skill minus old_skill held-out pass_rate exceeds the pooled stddev, the blind preference agrees, old_skill does not regress on the frozen 6-case guard, and tokens and time stay within old_skill's mean plus 1 stddev. If the delta stays within variance, as 2609.12742 found, or costs more for equal pass rate, refute GEPA for this requirement.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Narrow for this layer. Rules sync is already native. Claude Code 2.1.277 reads AGENTS.md when there is no CLAUDE.md, and .claude/rules keeps loading alongside it. The claude-md-and-agents-md mode skips an AGENTS.md that is already imported, and @path imports inside AGENTS.md are expanded. The stack's one-line CLAUDE.md -> @AGENTS.md is therefore the documented pattern. Skills are already single-sourced: 25 ~/.claude/skills entries are symlinks into ~/.agents/skills, installed by the pinned Vercel Skills CLI v1.7.0. The remaining activation-scoped gap is the per-skill invocation-policy pair the stack hand-tracks: lifecycle.md L155-157 and the manifest fields disable-model-invocation, upstream_allow_implicit_invocation, claude_listing and codex_enabled. rulesync v27 maps one root disable-model-invocation to Claude frontmatter and to Codex agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation:false (file-formats.md L990-997, L1300). It writes codexcli skills to .agents/skills and ~/.agents/skills (L1302), the root the Skills CLI already owns, so the directory would have two managers. Skills are emitted natively for both clients (no simulated mark in supported-tools.md L13 and L17), so only descriptions preload. --simulate-skills folds skill bodies into rules and must stay off; simulated-features.md still names codexcli, which conflicts with the supported-tools table. The @-import chain would be replaced, not preserved. The documented shared-AGENTS.md path is claudecode includeRoot:false, and with delete it removes a root CLAUDE.md. Here that file's Claude-only sections (plugin/MCP activity checks, Compact Instructions) would need a non-root rule targeted at claudecode. @path import handling is undocumented in the three docs read, and code search returned 0 hits, so it is unverified, not refuted. Generated SKILL.md copies would also break the manifest's skill_md_sha256 byte pins. v27.0.0 arrived about 16 months after creation (2025-06-18), so pin an exact version. It was not run (read-only).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Dry run in a scratch worktree: rulesync import --targets claudecode,codexcli, then rulesync generate --dry-run (docs/guide/dry-run.md) for rules, skills, mcp, hooks and permissions. Promote it to targeted only if all of these hold: (1) CLAUDE.md content survives byte-for-byte, or includeRoot:false without delete leaves it untouched; (2) the generated or emitted skills keep a SKILL.md sha256 equal to manifest skill_md_sha256; (3) only descriptions preload in both clients, with the Claude /context skill-listing row and the Codex skills-budget warning unchanged; (4) the Codex agents/openai.yaml policy matches the manifest's per-skill state for every skill; (5) a second generate is byte-idempotent; (6) it coexists with Skills CLI ownership of ~/.agents/skills, or replaces it with fewer self-maintained files (tools/adoption/apply_claude_settings.py and the manifest sync) and zero semantic diff.

Both apply only under managed allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills; /status lists skills whose allowed-tools were ignored). This host has no managed settings (/etc/claude-code absent), so both fixes are inert here. This is permission scope, not activation scope. Read-only audit of every installed SKILL.md frontmatter: five user-scope Trail of Bits skills, all symlinks into ~/.agents/skills, grant tools to themselves. fp-check: Read Grep Glob LSP Bash Task Write Edit AskUserQuestion TaskCreate TaskUpdate TaskList TaskGet. codeql: Bash Read Write Edit Glob Grep AskUserQuestion TaskCreate TaskList TaskUpdate TaskGet. supply-chain-risk-auditor: Read Write Bash Glob Grep. sarif-parsing: Bash Read Glob Grep. agentic-actions-auditor: Read Grep Glob Bash. The Codex skills, repo skills and the 5 enabled plugins declare none, and nothing in adoption/ or scripts/ reviews allowed-tools. (2) 2.1.282 L925-927 reserves the anthropic-skills and claude-ai namespaces; 2.1.283 L841 reverts the claude-ai part. (3) 2.1.283 L771 and L822 add /doctor prompt-audit, a native audit of CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents and commands that leads with stale paths, stale commands and contradicting instruction files. Use it before adding another pack. (4) 2.1.286 L472: a project or user skill named 'verify' now runs before commits (name-triggered activation); no installed skill has that name. (5) 2.1.287 L325-326 adds Claude Mods and the 'You should know' side agent; cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin is enabled in ~/.claude/settings.json, so count its side-agent usage. The mods reference (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/reference.md, as of v2.1.289) lists these events: prompt.compose returns system-prompt sections; prompt.section returning {text:null} omits a section; prompt.attachment returning {text:null} omits Claude Code's own messages; skill.prompt rewrites a skill's expanded text. Mods are therefore a native in-process lever for scoping per task, and also a new activation and supply-chain surface; the guard is allowManagedModsOnly. Whether the skill listing arrives as a section or an attachment was not verified. (6) 2.1.287 L391 (typed /skill names told to Claude); 2.1.290 L100 (the listing shows both names) and L155 (refuses '!' commands with control characters). (7) 2.1.277 L1255, just before the window, makes rules sync native by adding AGENTS.md support. Native levers the stack already uses: skillOverrides (2.1.129) and skillListingBudgetFraction. CODEX rust-v0.155.1 to rust-v0.160.1 (release notes): rust-v0.159.0 #48604 removed the bundled plugin-creator skill; the PR body says the skills context-budget warning test now expects six omitted skills instead of seven, so Codex omits skills past its budget. That is performance only, with no activation change. Scoping-relevant entries: #49127 (deduplicate skill listings before budgeting), #48353 (stable skill catalogs), #47350 (reuse cloud skill catalogs), #44655 (thread-level plugin exclusions), #45806 (plugin installs restricted to the root thread), #44701 (thread-scoped instructions), and #45764/#45769 (/usage shows plugin and skill activity, a native invoke-rate meter). rust-v0.160.1 has no skill or plugin entries. Wave 2 scored 10/12 vs 10/12; wave 3 scored 14/16 vs 14/16, with higher cost when the skill was forced ($1.79 vs $0.95, not isolated). Their standing rests on incumbency. output.notes:
This unit serves reproducible US-equities research and historical simulation through selectively loaded procedures. No installations, candidate execution, configuration changes, credential reads or trading actions occurred. API and page-fetch limits were reached; failed requests are included in counts.

Native-client findings: Claude 2.1.282 fixed repository/user/--add-dir skill pre-approval under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly; 2.1.284 separately fixed marketplace/claude.ai/npm plugin pre-approval, retaining exceptions for official or managed-trusted sources. Both fixes are already within the supplied installed 2.1.284 pin. They enforce permission policy, not catalog selection. Version 2.1.287 adds deeper plugin behavior through Mods; its built-in side agent requires explicit enablement and first-party telemetry-enabled sessions. That is no demonstrated solution to selective procedure loading. Additional relevant changes include broader AGENTS.md availability in 2.1.281, duplicate instruction-load fixes in 2.1.286–287, path-scoped rule loading on Write/Edit in 2.1.288, and instruction symlink/read-boundary fixes in 2.1.290. These are upstream findings, not installed-client verification. [Pinned changelog](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/v2.1.291/CHANGELOG.md).

Codex rust-v0.159.0 removes bundled plugin-creator (#48604), reducing one bundled procedure; this does not establish general plugin isolation. Rust-v0.160.0 caches parsed manifests (#49099), improving loading work without demonstrating reduced activation, and deduplicates cloud/executor skill listings before budgeting (#49127). The range also exposes thread-level plugin exclusions (#44655) as a relevant native acceptance-test lead. proposed.demonstrated_gap: No capability gap today. This adapter runs Claude Code through the Claude Agent SDK, using the existing Claude login, and reports each tool call as an ACP tool_call or tool_call_update. A tool call made inside a subagent keeps the tool_use id of the Agent/Task call that spawned it (src/tool-calls/renderer.ts:28-40; src/acp-agent.ts:6965-6979). The native path already provides that data: `claude -p --output-format stream-json` carries parent_tool_use_id, SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks carry agent_id, and the installed 2.1.291 offers `claude agents --json`. - openai/codex: latest stable rust-v0.160.1, published 2026-10-05T18:29:37Z. Prereleases rust-v0.161.0-alpha.13.1 and rust-v0.162.0-alpha.16 are out. Apache-2.0, 128,030 stars, newest commit 57d57df60845 at 2026-10-06. This host runs codex-cli 0.160.1, against the stack pin 0.160.0 and the verdict pin 0.155.1.
- Native command-center surfaces on the installed clients (help output only, not run):
  - `codex agents`: browses all sessions on the shared local app-server daemon; `--remote` accepts ws:// or unix:// addresses.
  - `codex remote-control`, `codex resume`, `codex fork`, `codex app-server`.
  - `claude agents --json [--all]`: prints active interactive and background sessions as JSON.
- Neither client's `--help` lists an ACP subcommand, so both reach ACP only through adapters.
- Incumbency: both winners stand on native_proven WSL receipts. macOS is untested. The research task had no matched baseline (open gap 2), so any quality ranking between the winners, or against alternatives, rests on incumbency.

2) USER-RELAYED CODE-MODE CONCERN (source review only; no lane was run).
Codex natively counts tool calls nested inside code-mode programs:
- registry.rs:680-689 at rust-v0.160.1 (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L680-L689) wraps every dispatch in log_tool_result_with_tags. The resulting codex.tool_result event carries tool_name, tool_namespace, call_id, duration and success (otel/src/tool_result.rs:54-74 on main).
- Nested calls carry ToolCallSource::CodeMode{cell_id, runtime_tool_call_id} (core/src/tools/context.rs:56-69 on main).
- They also emit codex.code_mode.nested_tool_dispatched on the codex_otel.trace_safe target (code_mode/mod.rs:358-365 at rust-v0.160.1). That event carries IDs only, not tool names.
- CODEX_ROLLOUT_TRACE_ROOT (rollout-trace/src/thread.rs:44,101-107 at rust-v0.160.1) records a local trace bundle. The installed 0.160.1 reduces it with the hidden command `codex debug trace-reduce`. The reducer links each nested call to its code cell (reducer/code_cell.rs:424-427; tool_dispatch_trace_tests.rs:194-211) and spans spawned child threads (thread.rs:43).
- Rollout and transcript viewers miss these calls because a CodeMode call returns a CodeModeResponse to the JS runtime, not a model-visible response item (tool_dispatch_trace.rs:94-110 on main).
- Docs: `[otel] exporter = otlp-http|otlp-grpc` sends codex.tool_result events (https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced.md).
- agentsview v0.44.0 release notes have no code-mode entry (https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/releases/tag/v0.44.0), so upgrading is not shown to fix the count.
- Unverified possible cause of the 'subagent' labels: agentsview's parser treats wait, spawn_agent and unnamed outputs as subagent activity (internal/parser/codex.go:2779-2803).
- Suggested native trial, with no new repository: on one code-mode lane, point `[otel]` at the observation-inference OTel collector, or set CODEX_ROLLOUT_TRACE_ROOT. Then compare codex.tool_result counts by tool_name and mcp_server with the main agent's in-program count.
- agentsview belongs to the observation-inference layer. wesm/agentsview now resolves to kenn-io/agentsview, an ownership move to note for supply chain.

3) SEEDED AND NOT PROPOSED.
- seeded_candidates is empty.
- Left to the agent-sdks layer:
  - claude-agent-sdk-typescript: v0.3.291, published 22 s before Claude Code v2.1.291 (lockstep with the CLI); no license; newest commit b95045e353da at 2026-10-06.
  - claude-agent-sdk-python: v0.2.163, 2026-09-30, MIT.
  - openai-agents-python: v0.23.1, 2026-10-02, MIT.
- The 2026-09-29 refutation of the SDKs in this layer stands. The native CLI already offers stream-json with parent_tool_use_id, hooks, resume and fork, and MCP custom tools.
- MoonshotAI/kimi-cli is archived (last release 1.52.0, 2026-09-22), so the staleness rule excludes it.
- qwen-code and crush are multi-provider clients, the class refuted on 2026-09-29 (opencode, goose, pi, jcode). The commits rule was not run on them, so their maintenance is unknown; they are not excluded.
- The refuted repositories were not re-assessed.

4) METHOD AND LIMITS.
- semble did a read-only code search over the public default branches of codex, agentsview, claude-agent-acp and letta-code. No candidate code was installed or run. File:line citations marked 'main' come from that 2026-10-06 index.

- Not covered: closed-source vendor desktop and cloud clients, paid CLIs (Cursor, Amp, Factory), mobile and remote wrappers, macOS behaviour.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: FIRST-PARTY SURFACE OF WINNER, not a third-party client: codex-rs/app-server with codex-rs/app-server-daemon and `codex remote-control` [experimental] at rust-v0.160.1. The sealed verdict and the 2026-09-23 receipt qualified only `codex exec resume` after a clean exit (N=1, WSL, 0.155.1). Kill-mid-turn recovery, independent-host continuation (open_gap 4) and macos-arm64 are unqualified. App-server is the protocol the TUI and Codex Desktop themselves run on (README L116-118), so a structured-event and application-state surface already exists on the native path with the same ChatGPT account: JSON-RPC over stdio, ws:// or unix://; thread/start, thread/resume and thread/fork; thread/read with runtime status notLoaded|idle|systemError|active; thread/items/list item-anchor pagination (#48151, rust-v0.159.0), which can verify item continuity after a kill. Cross-host: the ChatGPT desktop app starts the remote app server over SSH, and the CLI manages an app-server daemon with remote control. Since the sealed pin, rust-v0.160.0 shipped reconnect and remote-topology fixes on this path: #49105 resumes unsent queued TUI input after a reconnect without duplicate sends; #49144/#49161/#49171 make the TUI honor app-server provider and settings and list the correct sessions in resume and fork history; #49160 restores saved permissions on resume; #49084 tracks app-server running turns incrementally. These bear on open_gap 4 (remote topology), not on crash durability of `codex exec resume` (open_gap 0).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On WSL at the installed 0.160.0 (rust-v0.160.1 only backports Windows remote MCP environment preservation, #51121), same ChatGPT account, frozen research task, N>=3 per arm. Arm A: `codex exec resume`. Arm B: `codex app-server` thread/resume. SIGKILL the process mid-turn during tool calls, then resume. Score items restored (thread/items/list against the rollout file), lost or duplicated inputs, per-turn model and reasoning-effort records (open_gap 3), and effect checks (files, tests). Then, from the M5 Pro ChatGPT desktop app over an SSH remote connection to the WSL host, resume the same thread id. Precondition, unverified: WSL2 reachable by SSH from the Mac with codex on the login-shell PATH. Qualify app-server as the event and recovery surface if B matches or beats A on every check and the cross-host resume succeeds. Refute if resume loses items, a needed field requires experimentalApi, or the schema generated from the installed binary (`codex app-server generate-json-schema`) disagrees with the docs on a method the trial uses.

The open_gap 1 receipt resumed only after a clean exit (N=1, user/plugin MCP set, not the full project set). Resume fixes that the installed 2.1.284 lacks: 2.1.288, --resume dropping files a compaction had restored and a resumed session not saving a turn's last response (L242-243); 2.1.290, replies from `claude agents` retried while a crashed background session restarts (L80), and idle background sessions resuming their conversation after a restart (L121). Fixes already in 2.1.284 that no receipt has exercised: 2.1.281, a session that ended during a tool call resumes with the outcome marked unknown (L967); 2.1.282, resumed sessions no longer re-send earlier messages in a changed form (L870). Remote Control is continuation, not recovery: the docs say the local process must keep running.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Session supervisor around the installed claude and codex binaries (`happy claude`, `happy codex`, a daemon that spawns sessions, `happy resume`) with mobile, web and desktop apps and end-to-end encryption. Its gap over the winners has closed: both first-party clients now give same-account cross-device control of a host session (Claude Code Remote Control; Codex remote connections and `codex remote-control` [experimental]) plus native session lists (the agents view; the Codex agent command center). Decisive fit reasons: (1) it adds a third-party account (key-pair authentication, happy-cli README L95) on top of the native accounts; (2) its default relay is https://api.cluster-fluster.com (L128), though it is configurable through HAPPY_SERVER_URL and the server is open source in packages/happy-server (README L91), so the relay alone is not the reason; (3) a hand-off 'restarts the session in remote mode' (README L75), which puts a restart on the resume path where the open gaps sit, whereas Remote Control keeps the same process. Its CLI also bundles claude-agent-sdk for the Claude path (happy-cli README L86). Whether the vendor's Agent SDK authentication guidance applies to that use is not established and is not a reason here. Maintenance is active (default-branch commit 2026-10-05T22:09:43Z; cli-1.2.5 on 2026-09-22; 0 published repository advisories), so this is a fit rejection, not a maintenance one.

North-star action: qualify reliable native coding and bounded research for US-equities historical simulation; no trading, installation, candidate execution, credential access or configuration changes occurred. Comparisons above are proposed, not completed.

Winner health: both repositories remain unarchived under their existing canonical owners. Current releases are recorded above. No relicensing conclusion was established. The supplied native_proven evidence supports usability, not a measured quality ranking; both winners should remain comparison controls. Follow-up receipts marked advanced were not independently reread, so this response neither closes nor resets those gaps. Installed clients could not be inspected in this web-only lane; no local capability-absence claim is made.

No model-quality comparison was measured.

Local-model routes were examined without proposing serving repositories. Codex’s [documented OSS mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-advanced) selects Ollama or LM Studio; both provider directories exist at [rust-v0.160.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs). [Ollama’s Anthropic compatibility documentation](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api/anthropic-compatibility.mdx) describes Claude Code/local-server routing but only partial Messages compatibility, including incomplete tool-choice, deferred-tool and hosted-search support. These warrant separate client-protocol checks on the RTX 4090 and M5 hosts; serving/model/quantization selection belongs to observation-inference. Claude [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control) is unavailable with a non-Anthropic base URL, so local inference and native Remote Control are separate comparison arms.

Recovery boundary: remote access, process restart, persisted history, independent-host recovery, power-loss durability and provider-side cancellation are distinct claims. No retrieved evidence qualifies all of them. A local interruption acknowledgment does not establish cessation of provider billing. All macOS acceptance remains pending execution on the specified hosts.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: No winner records which agent, model and session wrote each changed line. After a squash merge, neither a PR reviewer nor the command-center orchestrator can separate agent-authored lines by lane or audit them. git-ai writes line-level attribution into Git Notes on each commit (`git log --show-notes="ai"`) and carries it through squash, merge, rebase, stash and cherry-pick. Agents report the lines they wrote, so no heuristics are involved. It supports Claude Code and Codex, among others, and offers `git ai stats --json` and an open standard (git_ai_standard_v3.0.0). Prompts are kept out of Git after scanning and redaction; whether that store is local or hosted was not verified here, and the answer matters for the local-first rule. The comparison arm is entireio/cli (Entire). It links each commit to the full agent session through an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and refs/entire/checkpoints refs, with Codex captured via .codex/hooks.json. That is richer, but session data is pushed as refs (or to a separate repository via --checkpoint-remote), which would publish raw sessions on this public repository, and it has a high-severity advisory (GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf, 2026-08-20). This is commit-level provenance, not tool-call telemetry.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run it as an Inspect or Harbor task in a scratch clone: two concurrent lanes (one Claude Code, one Codex) produce at least 10 squash-merged PRs. Measure line-level attribution precision and recall after squash, checked against each lane's own edit record. Confirm that no prompt or transcript text leaves the host or lands in pushed refs; any leak disqualifies. Also measure hook overhead per commit, and whether a reviewer can answer 'which lines came from which agent and model' from git-ai notes or stats compared with Entire checkpoints. Adopt the tool with exact attribution and zero leakage; record neither if both leak or lose attribution on squash.

Mergiraf is the maintained, syntax-aware git merge driver that a fair comparison needs. Its languages page lists Python (*.py), JSON (*.json), YAML (*.yml, *.yaml), TOML with dedicated pyproject.toml support, and Bash. It has moved past the v0.19.1 record the critic cited: v0.20.0 was published on 2026-09-26, and the default branch had a commit on 2026-10-04. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Step 1, demand: replay this repository's own merge history, with the drivers off and then on (configured through git's gitattributes merge-driver mechanism), and count how often a line-level git conflict arises on JSON, YAML or Python files. Near zero means the slot stays empty, whichever driver wins. Step 2, a frozen parallel-writer fixture: the same JSON, YAML and Python files edited in two worktrees, built from the replayed conflicts plus a small set of seeded concurrent edits. Merge arms: plain `git merge` (ort) baseline, weave v0.5.4, Mergiraf v0.20.0. proposed.demonstrated_gap: Worktrunk's open question is crash cleanup without deleting unrelated or dirty state (the 2026-09-23 jj record), and it remains unanswered. jj main now answers it natively. At 320f7e6b, CHANGELOG [Unreleased] says `jj workspace remove` 'removes a workspace and its directory from disk. The working-copy state is snapshotted into a commit before removal' (lines 56-57). `jj workspace add --colocate` creates a Git worktree alongside the workspace, and `jj workspace forget` removes it (lines 50-54). That keeps git-only tools (gh, difftastic, plain git) working inside each agent's workspace. `jj undo` of `jj workspace forget` preserves the recorded path (lines 120-122), and cross-workspace undo requires `--allow-cross-workspace` (lines 29-31). The 2026-09-23 refutation rested only on #9941 and `jj workspace remove` being unreleased. That is still literally true: no tag exists after v0.45.1, and #9941 merged on 2026-09-04, a day after v0.45.1. The sweep rule allows pinning a branch commit when the needed change exists only on the branch, and upstream documents a main-branch install. Prerequisite: git >= 2.42.0, because `jj workspace add` now uses `git worktree add --orphan` (lines 15-17). The WSL host has git 2.53.0. git >= 2.42 on the Macs is unverified.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: GitButler is the strongest agent-aware front end that replaces per-agent worktrees, and until now it had been weighed only as a dispatch framework. Both `crates/but` ('A GitButler CLI tool') and `crates/but-agentlog` ('Capture coding-agent session logs into Git metadata') ship at the release/0.22.3 tag, so a trial needs no master commit pin. `but oplog restore <sha>` restores the workspace to any snapshot, and 'Restorations create a new oplog entry before running'. That answers worktrunk's crash-cleanup question differently from jj. The vendor blog shows Claude Code lifecycle hooks giving each simultaneous session in one working directory its own branch. It does not meet this layer's requirement as written ('Own Git worktrees'), and it collides with other lanes in a shared checkout. GitButler moves HEAD to `gitbutler/workspace`, a merge commit it rebuilds, rewrites the index to the union of the applied branches, and 'If you switch to another branch, GitButler will need to be reinitialized'. Plain-git writers in the same checkout (Codex CLI, gh, worktrunk hooks) would conflict with it. Only Claude Code has evidence of hook attribution; Codex was not verified. It writes normalized_sha256 into the receipt, but no file in scripts/, tests/ or .github/ other than the verifier reads it back, and a failure is a one-line require() message. A deterministic cross-version regression that keeps 902 fills and 431.00 USD therefore passes; examples are a shifted fill timestamp, an offsetting price swap or a changed commission string. A caught regression carries no row-level evidence. dataframe_regression keeps the expected CSV in the repository. On mismatch it prints a comparison table of obtained versus expected values and their differences for the failing rows, using per-column np.isclose tolerances (v2.11.0 L132-L168; check(data_frame, basename, fullpath, tolerances, default_tolerance) at L197). num_regression covers numeric arrays. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Freeze one NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 quickstart output (seed 42; fills.csv 902 rows, positions.csv 451, account.csv 903). Apply at least 10 seeded regressions to copies: a 1-ns fill timestamp shift, an offsetting price swap that keeps realized PnL 431.00, a commission string change, a dropped-plus-duplicated fill that keeps the count, a column rename and a dtype change. Add at least 5 benign perturbations: regenerated UUIDv4 ids, float noise inside tolerance, and a re-run on the same pin. Arms: the current verifier as control, dataframe_regression, ApprovalTests.Python, and syrupy with path_type matchers. Metrics: seeded catch rate; false-failure rate on the benign set; whether the failure names the row, column, obtained value and expected value; and the commands or lines needed to accept an intended change. Adopt it only if it catches every seeded regression the control misses with zero benign false failures. It loses to ApprovalTests.Python on a tie, because ApprovalTests runs under python3 -m unittest.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The independent-observation part of the requirement has no transcript-analysis comparator. inspect_scout was proposed with split refuter verdicts and has never been run against an alternative on the same transcripts. Docent analyses agent runs through rubrics, clustering and DQL queries. It imports Inspect .eval logs with convert_inspect_eval_file_to_agent_runs and convert_inspect_directory_to_agent_runs, and also ingests Harbor/ATIF trajectories, so it can read the same logs inspect_scout reads. Positive evidence that it can be self-hosted: the repository root carries docker-compose.yml, docker-compose-db.yml, backend and frontend Dockerfiles and alembic migrations. The README's self-host guide link returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-06, and no self-hosting page surfaced in a search of docs.transluce.org/llms.txt. Footprint, recorded as facts: Postgres, Redis, three provider-key slots in .env.template (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY), and SENTRY_DSN and POSTHOG_API_KEY telemetry variables. Whether its LLM calls can route through the provider access the stack already has is unverified. There are no GitHub releases, so pin commit 8ab199c33218 (2026-09-04). Maintenance: 32 default-branch commits in 90 days. The license is NOASSERTION, recorded as information only.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Two pass/fail gates come before any scoring. Gate 1: it runs self-hosted on the WSL host without new provider keys, with its LLM calls going through existing provider access or the local gateway. Gate 2: with SENTRY_DSN and POSTHOG_API_KEY empty, no telemetry egress is observed. Failing either gate rejects it under the rules against new credentials and for local-first operation. If both gates pass, run a paired trial on the same retained Inspect .eval logs (or Harbor ATIF trajectories). Give the same K behaviour questions to inspect_scout scanners and to Docent rubrics, and score both against held-out human labels. Metrics: per-question precision and recall; the share of findings that cite a transcript location a reviewer can open; and setup footprint. Docent wins the comparator slot only with higher label agreement and no larger footprint. Otherwise it stays a recorded comparator.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Weighed as the PR-time LLM-security check that ships inside the promptfoo winner, and rejected. It reviews pull-request code for LLM-application vulnerabilities (prompt injection, PII exposure, excessive agency) and posts review comments, with optional SARIF output. Its analysis is hosted on the documented paths. The recommended Promptfoo Scanner GitHub App authenticates with GitHub OIDC after an email submission at promptfoo.dev. The manual path needs a Promptfoo Cloud account and an API token. The api-host input defaults to https://api.promptfoo.app. No model or provider input was found in the action README or in the GitHub Action docs input table; the code-scans CLI and the .promptfoo-code-scan.yaml config were not checked. Code diffs therefore leave the host and a new third-party account or token is required, and no demonstrated gap in this layer requires that. It is not a substitute for zizmor 1.30.1, which statically audits workflow YAML, or for the agentic-actions-auditor skill, which audits workflows that pass untrusted input to AI agents. It covers a third surface, application code, so rejecting it leaves those gates unchanged. Release cadence is healthy: the code-scan-action train has run since at least 0.1.5 (2026-04-14), within the 60 most recent monorepo releases. 0.2.1 (2026-10-06) is only a fix to dependency type definitions.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Two conditions together. First, a documented local path: api-host pointed at a self-hosted Promptfoo server, or code-scans run with a local or gateway provider. Second, a seeded trial on this repository's LLM-integrated scripts: N injected prompt-injection and excessive-agency paths across test PRs, compared against codeql and semgrep runs and the agentic-actions-auditor skill on the same PRs. Measure true findings, false positives and run-to-run stability of its LLM verdicts. Adopt it only if it finds seeded paths the others miss, at comparable precision, without sending code off the host.

Scope correction: Playwright already supports committed text and arbitrary binary snapshots. The gap is qualification of a Python/backtest oracle and its review cost, not an absent snapshot capability. Include its existing toMatchSnapshot implementation as a control. [Official documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots#non-image-snapshots). For snapshot trials, freeze data, engine/configuration and independently validated expected accounting results; seed dropped/duplicated fills, fee/sign/quantity errors and economically meaningful ordering changes. Preserve expected output, obtained output, diff, exit status and environment. Allowlist only genuinely incidental fields for normalization; never normalize away economic differences or regenerate expected outputs from mutants.

The old gaps marked settled were not reopened as missing work. The retained Promptfoo/Inspect receipt reports 30/30 agreement using a shared custom embedding-retrieval scorer and explicitly limits its claim to harness mechanics. It does not establish semantic-grader superiority. Thus the winners have integration evidence, but their standing as best for fresh semantic advice or backtest goldens remains unproven rather than earned by comparative evidence.
